agent.text:
Short answer
- Munich: Yes — Euro 5 diesels are allowed inside the city/Mittlerer Ring. Munich currently bans diesel Euro 4 and older only.  
- Stuttgart: Not always — Stuttgart has two bans. Euro 5 is allowed for the city‑wide (Euro 4 and older banned) but Euro 5 is banned inside the smaller inner “kleine Umweltzone” (inner districts/central area). So a Euro 5 diesel must avoid the small inner zone and use Park & Ride or outer streets.

What to do before you drive
- Fit a green Umweltplakette and write your plate on it — you need it to enter any German Umweltzone.  
- If you enter a banned area, the fine is €100 (processing typically makes it ~€128.50).  
- Carry your vehicle registration (Zulassungsbescheinigung) to prove the Euro class — the sticker alone does not show Euro standard.

Sources
- Stuttgart diesel ban info: Landeshauptstadt Stuttgart — https://www.stuttgart.de/en/leben/mobilitaet/dieselverkehrsverbot/dieselverkehrsverbot  
- Munich low‑emission zone (Mittlerer Ring) summary: Munich city low‑emission zone information.

agent.text:
You must have a valid Hungarian e‑vignette (e‑matrica) before driving on any tolled motorway. Cameras check plates; no valid vignette means a surcharge.

Key facts you can act on:
- Buy it before entry at ematrica.nemzetiutdij.hu or authorised resellers; enter your plate (no spaces) and the correct country code (RO for Romania). A wrong country code = no vignette. [ematrica.nemzetiutdij.hu]
- If you entered by mistake you have 60 minutes to buy retrospectively (otherwise you lose that option).  
- Surcharges (Decree in force from 2026): 27,790 HUF if paid within 60 days; 95,730 HUF if paid after 60 days. A lower differential surcharge applies if you had the wrong category (15,530 HUF / 49,190 HUF). Plate‑correction fee: 1,470 HUF. [Nemzeti Útdíj rates & rules — PDF and pages]  

Sources: official e‑vignette pages and tariff PDF [Nemzeti Útdíj — https://nemzetiutdij.hu/en/e-vignette/tolls/e-vignette-rates] and the published price/penalty PDF (2026) [https://nemzetiutdij.hu/api/uploads/e_matrica_arak_2026_pdf_611db0ecc1.pdf].

results.why: Romania ties the rule to road conditions; a Hungarian agency page says otherwise.

agent.text: No — Romania does NOT have a fixed 1 November–31 March winter-tyre rule. Winter tyres are required whenever public roads are covered with snow, ice or black ice (i.e. a condition-based obligation, any date of the year). Tyres must carry M+S (M.S., MS, M&S) — “all‑season” only tyres do not qualify. If you drive on snowy/icy roads without winter tyres you face a Class IV fine (9–20 penalty points; since 1 Jul 2026 one point = 216.25 RON → 1,946.25–4,325 RON) and the police may retain the vehicle registration certificate. See the Interior Ministry clarification: https://www.mai.gov.ro/precizari-privind-anvelopele-de-iarna/ (summary in the Drum Bun dataset).

baseline.text: No. In Romania the duty is tied to wintry road conditions (snow, ice or black ice) on any date — there’s no fixed calendar period. Tyres marked M+S (M.S., MS, M&S) count; tyres marked only “all seasons” do not.

agent.text:
Short answer — if the 10‑day digital vignette has already started, you cannot change the plate. A plate typo is treated as "no vignette" and may trigger the substitute toll (Ersatzmaut) for cars — €200 (effective 1 Jan 2026). If the Ersatzmaut is not paid on the spot, a court fine of €300–€3,000 can follow. You can still check whether the plate registered matches the vignette at the public evidence site: evidenz.asfinag.at.

What to do now
- Immediately verify your plate at https://evidenz.asfinag.at (enter plate + country). [ASFINAG](https://www.asfinag.at/maut-vignette/vignette/digitale-vignette/)  
- If you discover the typo before using tolled roads: cancel/replace before validity starts next time — corrections before start are free.  
- If you are stopped on a tolled road and have a wrong plate, expect to be asked to pay the Ersatzmaut (€200 for cars) or face later fines. [ASFINAG — vignette rules and penalties](https://www.asfinag.at/maut-vignette/vignette/digitale-vignette/)

Sources: ASFINAG pages above and the Drum Bun dataset summary of penalties and vignette rules.
